facts.value: Social media started in the mid-1990s with the invention of platforms like Classmates.com and SixDegrees.com.

facts.value: SixDegrees was the first online service designed for people to connect using their actual names instead of anonymously.
facts.programme_association: Social and Cultural Analysis (Women and Gender Studies) - BA

facts.value: SixDegrees included features like profiles, friends lists, and school affiliations.
facts.programme_association: Social and Cultural Analysis (Women and Gender Studies) - BA

facts.value: The platform's name SixDegrees was inspired by the six degrees of separation concept.
facts.programme_association: Social and Cultural Analysis (Women and Gender Studies) - BA

facts.value: In the early 2000s, social media platforms gained widespread popularity with BlackPlanet preceding Friendster and Myspace, followed by Facebook, YouTube, and Twitter.

facts.value: Research from 2015 reported that globally, users spent 22% of their online time on social networks.

facts.value: As of 2023, as many as 4.76 billion people used social media, which is about 59% of the global population.
